input.quote: ARTICLE IV TERM I Subject to termination pursuant to this Agreement, the Non Exclusive license granted by Licensor to Licensee shall be for an initial period of 36 months, commencing from the acceptance date, (the "Initial Period").
input.rationale: Article IV fixes a 36-month Initial Period and gives no Licensee (Customer) right to terminate for convenience; the only termination rights in the Agreement run to the Licensor (breach under Article IV and p0043, Change of Control/wind-up under Article XX) plus mutual insolvency termination (Article XIX). Absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under this rule, so it fails both the preferred (30 days' notice with pro-rata refund) and the fallback (60-90 days' notice with a fee capped at 3 months' fees). We therefore added the preferred Licensee convenience right with a prepaid-fee refund and confirmed the Licensor has no convenience right during the term (the Licensor does not currently have one, so that language is confirmatory only and not an additional ask).

ops.text: IV Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor, in which case Licensor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination, and no early termination fee or other penalty shall be payable by Licensee. Licensor shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Initial Period or any extension thereof.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article IV commits us to a 36-month term with no ability to exit for convenience, so we have added a 30 days' notice convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and confirmed the Licensor has no matching right during the term. If helpful, we can move to 60 days' notice.
proposal.summary: Add Licensee termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with prepaid-fee refund; bar Licensor convenience termination during the term.
